interpreter: python 3.12.16 (atlas-aci-dev-s16, docker only; no host python for project code)

notes: call fields: receiver, operator, method (identifier), arguments (argument_list), block (do_block|block)
do_block/block body field: body_statement (do) / block_body (braces); comments before the first statement are siblings of body, not children
pair: key (hash_key_symbol for `to:`; string for `"to":` and for hash rocket), value, anonymous `=>` token only in rocket pairs
string: children are anonymous quote tokens plus string_content / interpolation / escape_sequence; single-quoted `#{` stays one string_content
a lone `#@` yields TWO string_content children (a, #@) without interpolation, so the literal must be the source bytes between the delimiters
`%q(/a)` is a string whose delimiters are `%q(` and `)` (rejected by the quote check); `"/a" "/b"` is chained_string; heredoc is heredoc_beginning + heredoc_body; `%w()` is string_array
empty string has no string_content child
statement types seen: call, identifier (root), if_modifier, unless_modifier, unless, case, assignment
Rails.application.routes receiver is call(call(constant, application), routes); Blog::Engine.routes receiver contains scope_resolution
get("/a", to: "u#i") parenthesised call keeps the same argument_list named children

a heredoc body is a separate named sibling (heredoc_body) after the statement that owns the marker; the adapter skips heredoc_body like comment so it is not a spurious statement (the marker statement is non_literal_path)
field name for the call's argument list is `arguments` (not `argument_list`); the block field of a call is `block`; the draw body field is `body`
